In my view, in the light of this evidence of the doctor, the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability of the claimant at 20% to the whole body.
Hence, the whole body disability of the claimant is re-
assessed at 20% in this appeal.

4. As there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual income of the claimant, a sum of Rs.9,500/-
determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accidents of the year 2016 will have to be adopted.

As the claimant has suffered 20% disability to the whole body and since the claimant was aged 53 years as on the date of the accident, it would be appropriate to add 10% of the said income (Rs.950/-) as future prospects.

5. As the claimant was aged 53 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121,
a multiplier of '11' would have to be applied.

sentences.text: Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,37,940/- (Rs.10,450/- x 12 x '11' x 10%) towards loss of future earnings due to disability.
6. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities in life.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the claimant as suffered 20% disability to the whole body and was hospitalised for six days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities in life.
7. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,426/- towards medical expenses.
Since, the said award is based on the documentary evidence, same is affirmed.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards food and nourishment; a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards transportation charges and a sum of Rs.1,200/- towards attendant charges.

Since, the claimant was hospitalised for six days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.25,000/- in a lump sum under the head of conveyance, food and nourishment, attendant and other incidental charges, as against a sum of Rs.11,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.24,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period by taking the laid up period as three months.

Since the claimant has suffered left hip injury and injury to the left lower limb and having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, it would be appropriate to treat the laid up period as six months and award compensation towards 'loss of income during laid up period' at Rs.57,000/- (Rs.9,500/- x 6 months).
10.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who had deposed before the Tribunal has stated that the claimant would require a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- for the left hip replacement surgery.
However, no evidence is produced to indicate that the claimant had indeed undergone the said surgery.
Despite the same, in my view, interest of justice would be met if a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.
